cnd16:1.5: After hearing the nāga, they will depart from here.
cnd16:2.2: One who has left the abode: for the element of form, whatever desire, greed, relishing, and craving, and whatever attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies of the mind—these have been given up by the Buddha, the Blessed One, cut off at the root, made like palm stumps, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.
cnd16:2.7: for the element of consciousness, whatever desire, greed, relishing, and craving, and whatever attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies of the mind—these have been given up by the Buddha, the Blessed One, cut off at the root, made like palm stumps, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.
cnd16:3.2: Craving: craving for sights … craving for ideas.
cnd16:3.3: That craving has been cut off by the Buddha, the Blessed One, completely cut off, entirely cut off, stilled, calmed, made unable to arise again, and burned by the fire of knowledge.
cnd16:3.5: Imperturbable: perturbation is said to be craving.
cnd16:3.6: That which is greed, intense greed … covetousness, avarice, the unskillful root.
cnd16:3.7: That perturbation, that craving, has been given up by the Buddha, the Blessed One, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.
cnd16:3.9: Because perturbation has been given up, the Blessed One is imperturbable: he is not perturbed by gain, not perturbed by loss; not perturbed by fame, not perturbed by disrepute; not perturbed by praise, not perturbed by blame; not perturbed by pleasure, not perturbed by pain; he does not waver, tremble, quiver, or shake.
cnd16:3.15: Bhadrāvudha: this is that brahmin’s name … an expression—
cnd16:4.1: One who has left delight, crossed the flood, and is freed: delight is said to be craving.
cnd16:4.2: That which is greed, intense greed … covetousness, avarice, the unskillful root.
cnd16:4.3: That delight, that craving, has been given up by the Buddha, the Blessed One, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.
cnd16:4.5: One who has crossed the flood: the Blessed One has crossed the flood of sensual desire, crossed the flood of continued existence, crossed the flood of views, crossed the flood of ignorance, and crossed the whole path of transmigration; he has crossed, crossed over, completely crossed, gone beyond, completely gone beyond, and passed beyond.
cnd16:4.6: He has completed his stay, fulfilled his conduct … for him there is no transmigration through birth and death, no future rebirth—
cnd16:4.8: Freed: the mind of the Blessed One is liberated, freed, and well freed from greed; the mind from hate … the mind from delusion …
cnd16:4.9: the mind is liberated, freed, and well freed from all unskillful choices—
cnd16:5.6: For the Buddha, the Blessed One, formulation through craving has been given up, and formulation through views has been let go.
cnd16:5.7: Because formulation through craving has been given up and formulation through views has been let go, therefore the Buddha is one who has left formulation.
cnd16:5.8: I beseech: I beg, I beseech, I request, I consent, I long for, I yearn for, I wish for, I hanker for.
cnd16:5.10: Whatever is wisdom, understanding … non-delusion, investigation of principles, right view.
cnd16:5.11: The Blessed One has approached, closely approached, come to, fully come to, arrived at, fully arrived at, and is endowed with this intelligence, this wisdom.
cnd16:6.1: After hearing the nāga, they will depart from here.
cnd16:6.3: The Blessed One does no wrong (āgu), thus he is a nāga; he does not go, thus a nāga; he does not come, thus a nāga … in this way the Blessed One does not go, thus he is a nāga.
cnd16:6.4: After hearing the nāga, they will depart from here: having heard your word, speech, teaching, instruction, and advice, having heard, listened, learned, retained, and recognized it, they will depart from here, go, set out, and travel in every direction—
cnd16:9.2: Various people: aristocrats, brahmins, peasants, menials, householders, renunciates, gods, and humans.
cnd16:9.3: Gathered from the nations: the people of Aṅga, Magadha, Kaliṅga, Kāsi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Cetiya, Vaṁsa, Kuru, Pañcāla, Maccha, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Yona, and Kamboja.
cnd16:9.4: Gathered: gathered, come together, congregated, and assembled—
cnd16:10.1: Wishing for your word, O hero.
cnd16:10.3: The Blessed One is a hero because he is energetic, a hero because he is capable, a hero because he is powerful, a hero because he is able, and also a hero because he is free of goosebumps.
cnd16:12.1: Wishing for your word, O hero: your word, speech, teaching, instruction, and advice.
cnd16:12.2: Wishing: wishing, desiring, consenting, longing, yearning, and hankering—
cnd16:13.2: Them: those aristocrats, brahmins, peasants, menials, householders, renunciates, gods, and humans.
cnd16:13.4: Answer well: explain well, teach, assert, establish, clarify, analyze, disclose, and reveal—
cnd16:14.1: For truly you have known this Dhamma: for truly this Dhamma has been known by you, weighed up, examined, clarified, and made clear—
cnd16:17.1: Dispel all craving for taking up: craving for taking up is said to be craving for sights …
cnd16:17.2: As for craving for taking up: for what reason is it called craving for taking up?
cnd16:17.3: By that craving they take up, grasp, seize, adhere to, and insist on form.
cnd16:17.13: they take up, grasp, seize, adhere to, and insist on the cycle.
cnd16:17.15: Dispel all craving for taking up: they should dispel, completely dispel, give up, get rid of, eliminate, and obliterate all craving for taking up—
cnd16:17.18: Bhadrāvudha: the Blessed One addresses that brahmin by name.
cnd16:17.19: Blessed One: this is a term of respect … a designation based on realization, that is, Blessed One—
cnd16:18.1: Above, below, across, and in the middle.
cnd16:18.4: Across and in the middle: the present.
cnd16:18.7: Across and in the middle: the human world.
cnd16:18.10: Across and in the middle: neutral things.
cnd16:18.16: Across and in the middle: neutral feeling.
cnd16:19.1: For whatever they grasp in the world: whatever is included in form, feeling, perception, choices, or consciousness, they take up, grasp, seize, adhere to, and insist on.
cnd16:19.2: In the world: in the lower realms … in the world of the sense fields—
cnd16:20.1: Māra pursues that creature: by that very force of the choices of deeds, Māra of the aggregates, Māra of the elements, Māra of the sense fields, Māra of destinations, Māra of rebirth, Māra of relinking, Māra of existence, Māra of transmigration, and Māra of the cycle, bound up with relinking, pursues, follows, and becomes a follower.
cnd16:20.2: Creature: a being, a person, a man, a young man, a male, an individual, a living being, a jāgu, a creature, an indagu, a human—
cnd16:22.4: these people stuck in Death’s dominion.
cnd16:23.2: Therefore: for that reason, from that cause, with that as the condition, with that as the source, clearly seeing this drawback of craving for taking up—
cnd16:23.4: Understanding: knowing, understanding, comprehending, discerning, recognizing, and penetrating that “all conditions are impermanent” …
cnd16:23.5: “whatever is liable to arise, all of that is liable to cease,” knowing, understanding, comprehending, discerning, recognizing, and penetrating.
cnd16:23.6: Should not take up: one should not take up, grasp, seize, adhere to, or insist on form;
cnd16:23.16: one should not take up, grasp, seize, adhere to, or insist on the cycle—
cnd16:24.1: A mindful mendicant should not grasp anything at all in the whole world.
cnd16:24.2: Mendicant: either a virtuous ordinary mendicant or a mendicant in training.
cnd16:24.4: when the mendicant develops mindfulness meditation by observing an aspect of the body, they are mindful …
cnd16:24.7: Anything at all: whatever is included in form, feeling, perception, choices, or consciousness.
cnd16:24.8: In the whole world: in the whole world of the lower realms, the whole human world, the whole world of the gods, the whole world of the aggregates, the whole world of the elements, and the whole world of the sense fields—
cnd16:25.1: Seeing in this way those attached to taking up: those said to be attached to taking up are those who take up, grasp, seize, adhere to, and insist on form;
cnd16:25.11: they take up, grasp, seize, adhere to, and insist on the cycle.
cnd16:25.12: Iti: this is a joining of words … the sequence of words, that is, iti.
cnd16:25.13: Seeing: looking, observing, discerning, seeing, regarding, contemplating, and examining—
cnd16:26.1: These people stuck in Death’s dominion.
cnd16:26.2: People: this is a term for beings. Death’s dominions are said to be the corruptions, the aggregates, and the choices.
cnd16:26.3: People, in Death’s dominion, Māra’s dominion, the dominion of dying, are stuck, deeply stuck, thoroughly stuck, caught, snagged, and hindered.
cnd16:26.4: Just as an object is stuck, deeply stuck, thoroughly stuck, caught, snagged, and hindered on a peg in a wall or on an elephant’s tusk, in the same way people, in Death’s dominion, Māra’s dominion, the dominion of dying, are stuck, deeply stuck, thoroughly stuck, caught, snagged, and hindered—
cnd16:28.2: Sir, the Blessed One is my Teacher, and I am a disciple.
cnd16:28.3: The Exposition of the Questions of the Young Brahmin Bhadrāvudha, the twelfth.
